newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil firms may step up Iraqi crude buying.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil firms may step up Iraqi crude buying.

text.p: Japanese oil companies say they are thinking of making fresh purchases of Iraqi crude oil now that Baghdad has been given U.N. approval to export crude oil for another six months starting on Sunday.
Some oil traders said the oil firms might even make larger purchases than in the first six-month period, which started on December 10 and expires on Saturday.
"I think there's a chance that the volume will increase," a trader with a Japanese trading company said.
He said interest in Iraqi crude was strong because prices were competitive compared to other similar crude grades.

Under the terms of the first six months, Iraq's Basrah Light price was linked to Oman and Dubai quotations, but the Iraqi grade is also similar in quality to Saudi Arab Light, which has sold at a 55-cent premium to Basrah Light.
Nippon Oil Co Ltd, one of the most aggressive Japanese buyers, said that it was "considering making purchases", in spite of recent problems with Iraqi deliveries.
In the first 180 days, the leading oil refiner was given approval to buy a total of two million barrels in two separate agreements.
Iraq, however, made a last-minute cancellation of Nippon Oil's second cargo of 900,000 barrels last week. Nippon Oil said it was not given a reason for the cancellation.
Traders said that the Iraqi crude had some disadvantages over the similar Saudi Arab Light, noting that the pumping rate of Basrah Light was slower, which meant longer loading hours.

However, even given these disadvantages, Basrah Light remained an attractive crude price wise if the current price formula was maintained, traders said. Industry sources said that this time, many Japanese oil refineries might negotiate directly with Iraq rather than have a trading company act for them, because this would enable them to cut commission costs.

The exception would be companies which made only small purchases, falling far short of filling a VLCC (Very Large Crude Carrier) which is capable of carrying more than 200,000 tonnes of crude oil, or about 1.8 million barrels.
Seven Japanese oil companies purchased Iraq's Basrah Light for delivery in the oil deal's first 180 days.

Trading house Mitsubishi Corp -- acting on behalf of Nippon Oil, Japan Energy Corp, Kashima Oil Co, Showa Shell Sekiyu KK and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd -- bought a total of 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Basrah Light crude.
Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd and Cosmo Oil Co Ltd each purchased 900,000 barrels of Iraqi crude in direct negotiations with Iraq.

Under the United Nations plan implemented on December 10, Iraq was allowed to sell $2.00 billion worth of oil to buy food and medicine for its people, who have been suffering under sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Iraq invaded Kuwait.
